candidateEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Sol and Luna on September 22. Its release notes place them in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and say they are separate from the models in ordinary Chat.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: We’re introducing GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in ChatGPT Work and Codex. These models are separate from the models available in Chat.
Available models and reasoning effort options depend on your plan and workspace settings.

scopeAndFreshness: Release notes state Sol and Luna are introduced in ChatGPT Work and Codex and are separate from models available in Chat, matching the article's attributed sentence; the release adds Free/Go desktop access to Luna, an omission that does not contradict the claim.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI also lists lower API prices. An API is the developer-facing connection that lets software send work to a model and pay for the text it processes. Those figures are not a ChatGPT subscription price.
A model picker is the list of AI models an account can choose. The AI Fundamentals 101 lesson on tokens explains why text processed can be a usage meter rather than a monthly subscription price.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex starting today for all Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users. Free and Go users can access GPT‑6 Luna in the desktop app. These models are not yet available in Chat.
Prices are per 1 million tokens. GPT‑6 Sol can take on difficult work tasks while giving you more room to iterate with higher usage limits and lower cost.

scopeAndFreshness: The release lists prices per 1 million tokens, which is API usage metering; the article correctly explains this and its negative claim that the figures are not a ChatGPT subscription price follows directly from that per-token framing.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI says model and reasoning choices depend on a plan and workspace settings. A workspace is a shared work account whose plan and settings can affect which model choices appear. Its rollout is gradual, so an announcement cannot show what a particular account can select.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: We’re introducing GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in ChatGPT Work and Codex. These models are separate from the models available in Chat.
Available models and reasoning effort options depend on your plan and workspace settings.

scopeAndFreshness: The release notes state verbatim that available models and reasoning effort options depend on plan and workspace settings; the article attributes this to OpenAI and adds the rollout caveat consistent with source limitations.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI says GPT-6 Sol can take on difficult work tasks. For a routine email, summary or document draft, another available model may be a sensible alternative; compare it with Sol or Luna in your own service before treating a new name as an automatic upgrade.
OpenAI’s performance and cost comparisons are its own evaluation claims. They do not promise that a particular task will be faster, cheaper or better for you.
